newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins set record after Fed mtng,job data.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins set record after Fed mtng,job data.

text.p: Prices of all Russian MinFin bonds hit historic highs on market relief after the Federal Reserve declined to change interest rates and unemployment data which boosted U.S. Treauries, dealers said on Thursday.

The U.S. Labour Department said on Thursday 217,000 overall non-farm jobs were added to payrolls in June, up from 166,000 new jobs in May. But non-government job growth slowed to 151,000 last month from 180,000 in May, it said.
"The rise started after the news, right on the back of stronger Treasuries," one dealer said.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had expected the report to show the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.8 percent, and an increase of 220,000 in non-farm jobs.
Dealers disagreed on the trend for the bonds which have been slowly rising over the last month, generally tracking U.S. Treasuries.

Dealers said prices had edged up in early trading as the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) decided late on Wednesday to keep interest rates unchanged but they added buying was mixed with profit-taking on the priced-in news.
"Unchanged (interest) rates had no big impact on prices," Most Bank dealer Alexander Rodionov said. "Prices firmed further after the (U.S. June unemployment data)."
MinFins, along with other emerging debt, are sensitive to any news suggesting a change in U.S. interest rates and U.S. Treasury bond prices.
